findings: C is the key: "the figure he writes down is the fraction he needs in front of him before he can smell anything" - the number is the gas-in-air share at first detection.

A dies on "three at the cottage nearest the vessel, five at the farm office halfway up, eleven at the bungalow": the figure RISES as the warning weakens, and since "He is working to four", eleven is a bad figure, not a good one.
B dies on "The box counts in parts of gas to a thousand parts of air": the quarter-turns are how he opens the valve, not what he records.
D dies on "opens its needle valve a quarter-turn at a time and sniffs at the funnel until the smell arrives": the figure is measured at the nose, not computed from pipe length.
justification: Arithmetic check: target four parts per thousand = 0.4 percent, and "a fifth of the leanest mixture of propane and air that will burn" (propane LFL 2.1 percent) gives 0.42 percent - the figures reconcile.

findings: A is the key: "Some is oxidised on contact into a disulphide, a serviceable molecule that is no use as a warning, because it hardly smells" - partly changed into a compound the nose can hardly pick up.
B dies on "put into the gas at the depot at a fixed weight to a fixed volume".

C dies on the timing: the oxide is already there before service - "a bloom of rust from the weeks the lengths stood in the yard" - and "Bare oxide takes the most, so a main scrubs hardest in the week it goes into service", i.e. the taking is greatest at the start and stops with age, not once corrosion begins in service.
D dies on "the gas that leaves the far end has less smell in it than the gas that went in": the loss is in the pipe, not at the cooker.
justification: Only A matches the two stated fates of the mercaptan (sticking and oxidation to a near-odourless disulphide); C inverts the passage's age relation.

findings: D is the key: "Once a stretch of wall has taken all it can hold it stops taking, and the gas goes past unchanged" plus "reads three at both ends" for a line in service "since the sixties".
A dies on "is longer than the new run".
B dies on "is the same bore".
C dies on "comes off the same vessel and the same fill".
justification: The passage deliberately equalises length, bore, vessel and fill so that only saturation with age explains the flat three-to-three reading.

findings: B is the key by both support and elimination: "The soak ends when the readings say it has ended, which means walking the run again", and the closing walk (figure six, against a target of four) shows the criterion is a re-walk, not a calendar date.
A dies twice: "holding the system at three or four times the ordinary dose" (not the ordinary dose) and "What he cannot do is put a date on the end of it in advance".
C dies on "costs more than the odorant does": one call-out outweighs the odorant, so the odorant is not the main cost.
D dies on "and you do it before the first burner is lit".
justification: B's wording about a second walk of the run is looser than "walking the run again", but the ending criterion it states is the passage's own and the other three options are each contradicted outright, so B stands.

findings: D is the key: "every joint was pressure-tested, the paperwork is signed" yet eleven parts per thousand are needed before the smell arrives, and "The slope is not a fault in the pipe and it is not a fault in the fill".
A dies on "it is not a fault in the fill" plus "put into the gas at the depot at a fixed weight to a fixed volume".
B dies on "the gas that leaves the far end has less smell in it than the gas that went in": the warning does not survive the run.
C dies on "The pipe that needs watching is the pipe nobody has ever used" and "a main scrubs hardest in the week it goes into service".
justification: The whole piece is built on a clean-tested new main delivering under-odorised gas, which is exactly D.

findings: D (Worse) is the key: the gap sits at the top of an escalating indictment - "for eight minutes none of the three adults living there could turn the water off", then "none could say which side of the path", then a tenure that is "long enough to have asked" - and a bare Worse ranks an additional aggravating fact.
A (Nowadays) dies on "There is nothing unusual in that house, and nothing modern about it either": no then-versus-now contrast is in play.
C (Happily) dies on polarity - "The hall carpet took most of the damage".

B (Oddly) is the near miss and the reason this gap is not a walkover: as a disjunct it would predicate oddness of the residence itself, whereas the clause "which is long enough to have asked" supplies a reproach, i.e. a ranking of badness rather than a surprise.
justification: Closest call of the three sentence-adverb gaps; Worse fits the escalation and the scope of the following relative clause, Oddly misattaches.

findings: A (witness) is the key: the apposition defines it - "somebody who was in the right room on the right morning and has answered questions ever since" - and the next paragraph repeats "by being in the room when it happens".
B (recruit) dies on "This competence is not earned and not handed out": nobody is enlisted.
C (caretaker) dies on "The knowledge holds no office and is not bought with the house".
D (lodger) dies on "It may sit with the owner, the owner’s daughter, or the man who rents the back bedroom": the lodger is one possible holder, not the category.
justification: The gloss after the colon is a definition of witness - presence, not appointment.

findings: B (caught) is the key: "the way a cold is, by being in the room when it happens" - colds are caught.
A (issued) dies on "This competence is not earned and not handed out".
C (bought) dies on "The knowledge holds no office and is not bought with the house".
D (chosen) dies on "Nobody else will have it, because there is nothing in it to have": no selection is involved.
justification: The simile fixes the verb: contagion, not issue, purchase or choice.

findings: A (address) is my answer: every predicate in the gloss takes a designating expression as subject - "It names one thing in one building and explains nothing; most are four words long; nobody disputes them" - and “the one behind the coats” is exactly an address for a valve, valid in one building only.

B (instance) is the reason this line is flagged rather than passed clean: it is defensible against "no rule, no principle" read as the general-versus-particular contrast, but an instance does not "name" and is not "four words long", and an instance presupposes the general the passage has just denied.
C (opinion) dies on "nobody disputes them".
D (anecdote) dies on "most are four words long" and "explains nothing": four words is no anecdote.
justification: Narrowest margin in the unit; A wins on the predicate-type test (names / word length / undisputed) but B survives a general-versus-particular reading well enough to be worth the resolver's attention.

findings: C (commonplace) is the key: the concession needs a property that ought to make the knowledge spread easily - "Nothing on that list is difficult and nothing on it is being kept back. Ask, and you will be told gladly and at length, and still have nothing".
A (privileged) dies on "nothing on it is being kept back".
B (perishable) breaks the concession: perishability is another reason it fails to travel, not something "Although" can concede against one-way transmission.
D (technical) dies on "Nothing on that list is difficult".
justification: Although-clause demands an ordinariness concession, which only commonplace supplies.

findings: D is the key and is quoted outright: "The last octave comes in over somebody’s left hand, two octaves down, and that’s what it has to agree with".
A dies on "she played a dozen notes into her meter, the last of them from the top octave" and on the curve covering "all eighty-eight notes": the sample reaches the top and the curve does not stop.
B dies on "this upright’s figure is larger than a grand’s, its short thick strings already counted in it": the small instrument's stiffness is already in the figure.
C dies on "The extra cents are not an allowance for the cold".
justification: Physics reconciles: the fourth partial is two octaves above the fundamental, so "A note down in the tenor has its fourth partial about nine cents sharp" and the treble note two octaves up landing nine cents wide are the same fact.

findings: A is the key: every day on the card is that town's market day - "Haddenthorpe has kept its Monday market since a charter of 1227, and Nerresby has held a Tuesday one for as long" and "Thrapmere fills on a Wednesday and Lower Shenwold on a Thursday".
B dies on "The Shenwolds sit three miles off that road, up a lane the coaches did not use": a place off the road is still on the card, so the road did not settle inclusion.
C dies on "Upper Shenwold has no market of its own".
D dies on "the Thursday market is the largest of the four".
justification: Mileage reconciles and supports A: Nerresby is nine miles from Haddenthorpe and "Thrapmere stands thirty miles from Nerresby, and the road to it runs back through Haddenthorpe and twenty-one miles beyond" (9 + 21 = 30), so the Tuesday-to-Wednesday leg doubles back - an order no route-planner would choose, and the 1227 charter predates the 1769 turnpike by five centuries.

findings: B är nyckeln: "Den översta bokstaven är 73 millimeter, nästa rad 36" och "Det första steget halverar alltså bokstavshöjden" - 37 mm är det största steget, både absolut och relativt.
A dör på "Storlekarna följer ingen jämn trappa".
C dör på "mellan de två nedersta raderna skiljer det åtta tiondels millimeter" - 0,8 mm mot 37 mm högst upp.
D dör på "Sedan blir stegen kortare": stegen krymper hela vägen nedåt, så mitten är aldrig störst.
justification: Siffrorna går ihop: 73 till 36 är en halvering, och 0,8 mm på en rad som är "drygt sju millimeter" hög är ungefär en tiondel, precis som texten säger.

findings: C är nyckeln: "beror inte på hur många millimeter som skiljer tecknen åt, utan på hur stort det avståndet är i förhållande till tecknet självt".
A dör på "Två små bokstäver med ett litet mellanrum trängs lika mycket som två stora med ett stort".
B dör på "Den sitter inte i ögats upplösning: näthinnan skiljer ut tecknet".
D dör på "Trängseln växer alltså nedåt på arket i takt med att bokstäverna krymper" - den avtar inte.
justification: Texten definierar trängsel som ett förhållande, inte ett millimetertal, och D är en ren riktningsvändning.

findings: D är nyckeln: "Det är inte de fjorton raderna som tar tid, utan de sjuttio tecknen: var och en ska höras och prickas av".
A dör på "Ingen rad prövas om".
B dör på samma mening: "Det är inte de fjorton raderna som tar tid".
C dör på "Även ett barn som stannar högt upp tar längre tid än förut" - fördröjningen sitter inte längst ned.
justification: Tidsangivelserna går ihop: fyrtio barn på två timmar är tre minuter styck, och 120 minuter delat på sju ger sjutton barn.

findings: A är nyckeln: "Nedgången i kurvan ligger på det året" och "utan mellan två på varandra följande årgångar", med bytet "under höstterminen 1978".
B dör på "de mäter alltså inte samma sak" och "Som en enda kurva över barns syn i en svensk stad går den inte att läsa".
C dör på "Gränsen 0,8 ändrades inte vid bytet".
D dör på "samma steg finns i de tre distriktens siffror var för sig".
justification: Årtalen går ihop: 1961-1996 är trettiosex årgångar, sjutton före bytet (1961-1977) och nitton efter (1978-1996), vilket lägger brottet exakt vid höstterminen 1978.

findings: D är nyckeln: "Jag begär något annat: att stämman beslutar två saker i samma beslut" - först uttagen, "Sedan i vilken ordning bilarna får ström de nätter då sju är fullt".
A dör på "Delar vi fyrtiofem lika på tio bilar blir det fyra och en halv på var, och då laddar ingen av de tio".
B dör på "Någon större huvudsäkring tänker jag därför inte begära i år".
C dör på "Att den ska stå skriven innan uttagen sitter uppe är däremot hela min poäng" - turordningen får inte skjutas till när den behövs.
justification: Amperetalen går ihop: 125 minus 80 ger 45, 45 delat på 6 ger 7,5 alltså sju bilar, och fyra stolpar à 32 ampere behöver 128 - därför är de snabba bara när tre står tomma.

findings: C är nyckeln: "styrelsens förslag står där som punkt sju".
A dör på "Kallelsen sitter med häftstift på anslagstavlan utanför tvättstugan".
B dör på "Punkten är en rad lång".
D dör på "Var de ska stå framgår inte".
justification: Alla tre felaktiga alternativ motsägs direkt av detaljer i samma stycke.

findings: D är nyckeln: "det skymmer inte sikten. Från gräset utanför ser man golvet från kant till kant", och räcket är "i knähöjd".
A dör på "inte byggt för att hålla någon ute".
B dör på "Räcket är det ursprungliga" med "Börje Ängman, 1934" skåret i virket.
C dör på "Insidan har sin gamla gröna färg i behåll".
justification: Räckets låga höjd bär hela textens poäng om offentlighet, och de tre andra alternativen motsägs var för sig.

findings: A är nyckeln: "Paret som kommer i fart mot ett hörn måste vrida nittio grader på två steg, eller stanna", medan "En rund bana har ingen sådan punkt" och "Den var lättare att gå runt i".
B dör på "utan tak och utan stolpar inne på golvet".
C dör på "Spelmännen satt på en låg scen vid ena kanten" och "längst bort på banan hördes de sämre" - avståndet är inte lika.
D dör på "Golvet ligger plant på sina syllar, och regnet rinner ner mellan brädorna".
justification: Texten avvisar uttryckligen billighetsförklaringen - "Rundningen var inte det billiga valet" - och lägger skälet i rörelsen runt varvet.
